question.text: Himalaya Mutual Fund wants to launch a 'Specialized Investment Fund' (SIF) - the new product line introduced by SEBI's amendment to the MF Regulations in December 2024. According to Section 2.4.2.4 of Chapter 2, what is the MINIMUM required investment amount from an investor in an SIF?

answer.text: Rs. 1 lakh across all investment strategies
Rs. 5 lakh across all investment strategies
Rs. 10 lakh across all investment strategies
Rs. 1 crore across all investment strategies

explanation.text: The Logic: Section 2.4.2.4 (p. 42) explicitly states that SIFs are "sophisticated mutual funds where the minimum required investment amount is Rs. 10 lakhs from the investors across all investment strategies." This was introduced via SEBI (Mutual Funds) (Third Amendment) Regulations, 2024 w.e.f. December 16, 2024. The Trap: Option A (Rs. 1 lakh) and Option B (Rs. 5 lakh) are not the workbook-cited SIF minimum. Option D (Rs. 1 crore) is the AIF minimum - a classic Cat III vs SIF swap. SIF is an MF-based structure at Rs. 10 lakh, NOT an AIF at Rs. 1 crore. Note: Comparisons with PMS entry points and Category III leverage, short-selling or performance-fee economics are not part of the cited SIF minimum on p. 42 and should be separately sourced before being relied upon.
